problem:
A particle $P$ moves in the $x$-$y$ plane (relative to a fixed origin $O$) with position vector

$$
r=⟨\frac{3(t-2)^{2}}{t+1},\frac{3(t-2)^{2}}{t+5}⟩,\,t\in [0,\infty ).
$$

Calculate the times at which the particle is stationary.

The particle is stationary at $t=$  
{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity vector $v.$ Differentiating the position vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{3(t-2)^{2}}{t+1}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{3(t-2)^{2}}{t+5})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3(t-2)(t+4)}{(t+1)^{2}},\frac{3(t-2)(t+12)}{(t+5)^{2}}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The particle is stationary when its velocity is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =0 \\ ⟨\frac{3(t-2)(t+4)}{(t+1)^{2}},\frac{3(t-2)(t+12)}{(t+5)^{2}}⟩ & =⟨0,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So we need

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3(t-2)(t+4)}{(t+1)^{2}}=0\, & ⇒\,3(t-2)(t+4)=0\,⇒\,t=2,-4, \\ \frac{3(t-2)(t+12)}{(t+5)^{2}}=0\, & ⇒\,3(t-2)(t+12)=0\,⇒\,t=2,-12.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $t=2$ is the only solution that satisfies both equations, so this is the only value of $t$ when the particle is stationary.
